question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x+y}}{2}, & \,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ for $0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{{e}^{x+y}}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}\cdot {e}^{y}\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}\cdot (2-1) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}, & \,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{e}^{x+y}}{2})}{(\frac{{e}^{x}}{2})} \\  & ={e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{y}, & \,0\le x\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
